summary.headline: VST Tillers guides no formal FY27 outlook; industry volume seen flat at 10–11 lakh tractors, with power tiller share at 70–75%.
summary.overview: Management declined formal FY27 guidance, citing inflation from the war and an El Niño-linked monsoon risk, and will review performance quarter by quarter. April was better than last year and May satisfactory, with June the key monsoon month. Price hikes of about 1.5% passed through year to date, with cost reductions of 2–3%, and management warned that continued inflation would force more price increases and hit volumes. Growth levers cited are small farm machinery (power tillers, power weeders, electric variants), compact and higher-HP tractors via VST Zetor, a Netherlands setup for Europe, and a US launch timeline.

segments.name: Power tillers
segments.commentary: Market share ~70–75%; Chinese imports not permitted in this segment. Average price ~₹2 lakh; retail finance share expected to rise from ~10% to ~20% this year.

segments.name: Power weeders
segments.commentary: Market share only ~6–7%, entered two years ago; highly unorganised, import-dominated (China). Average price ~₹60,000.

segments.name: Tractors (domestic)
segments.commentary: Less than 1% national share; over 10% share in four-wheel-drive compact (<30 HP) segment in Maharashtra and Gujarat. Entered large tractors last year and is expanding into North India (Lucknow office).

segments.name: Europe / exports
segments.commentary: Business held flat; transit times rose from 30–45 days to 90–120 days due to the war, so Netherlands operations are being set up to speed delivery and inventory rotation.

segments.name: VST Zetor JV (higher HP)
segments.commentary: Piloted for ~1.5 years; to be scaled up meaningfully in FY27.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 guidance; performance to be assessed quarter by quarter and month by month.
Industry tractor volume expected around 10–11 lakh units and broadly flat this year unless new state schemes are announced; management would not rule out single-digit growth or a slight decline.

Plan of 3 new compact tractor platforms over 12–18 months (about 12–16 variants) and 2 higher-HP upgrades this year plus a new higher-HP platform towards year end; 16–20 product launches over 18 months.
US: tractor shipments by end-CY2026; market launch by end-CY2027 (analyst confirmed CY27, not FY27).
Electric tillers and weeders: commercialisation to scale from Q2 FY27.
Inorganic: evaluating adjacent opportunities globally and in India; expects to close at least one in roughly six months; will be an acquisition, not a JV.
risks_watch: June monsoon onset and rainfall distribution; rainfed areas most exposed to El Niño.
Continued inflation forcing further price hikes, which could dampen volumes.
Subsidy-driven demand pull-forward (e.g., Maharashtra last year) that may not repeat.
Export delays from war-related transit times until the Netherlands operations are running.
Above-50 HP volume decline under TREM V; timing of the 2028 interim norm.
Timing of electric tiller/weeder commercialisation from Q2 and the global tech centre (2027).
Acquisition target and closure in roughly six months.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on the near-term market, citing inflation, El Niño and monsoon risk, and declining to give formal guidance. More confident on the small farm machinery opportunity, product pipeline and the Europe and US expansion plans.
key_quotes: Given these uncertainties, we are not providing any formal guidance at this stage and will instead assess the situation quarter by quarter and month by month.

So overall we are able to manage our bottom lines healthily but like I said if this inflationary pressure continues then we will have to pass on more to the consumer and that will definitely affect demand and volumes.
In the power tiller segment, we hold a market share of around 70% –75%, and Chinese imports are not permitted in this segment.
I believe the industry volume is likely to remain around the 10–11 lakh range.

qa_highlights.question: How resilient is tractor demand given El Niño, low interest rates and GST benefits?
qa_highlights.answer: Rainfed areas will be hit hard by poor or late rain; irrigated areas may see cropping pattern shifts. Price hikes across the industry under inflation mean the volume lift from the GST cut is unlikely to sustain if inflation persists.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been taken YTD against raw-material inflation, and how much is still to come?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1.5% price increase passed through, power tiller prices up 2–3% (subsidy-linked), 2–3% cost reduction, plus TOC-driven efficiency. Bottom line is being managed, but further inflation would mean more pass-through and hit volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Is small-farm mechanisation at an inflection point, and what is the mid-term growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees a tremendous opportunity given 70–80% of Indian farmers are small and marginal; power weeder industry grew from ~2,000 units three years ago to ~11,500 last year, with the challenges being awareness, availability, accessibility, affordability and confidence.

qa_highlights.question: What are the electric weeder/tiller customer economics and payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Electric units give 4–5 hours of work per charge, similar to ICE usage; power tiller/weeder payback is about 2 years at 120 use-days, and electric payback should be faster as fuel cost is avoided.

qa_highlights.question: Which states could outperform this year given the low base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cannot predict which state will launch schemes; subsidies pull forward pent-up demand rather than add to the long-term trend. Industry expected flat at 10–11 lakh units; could be single-digit growth or slightly negative.

qa_highlights.question: What is the market share and pricing in power tillers and power weeders, and where is the tractor business strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Power tillers ~70–75% share with Chinese imports not allowed, ~₹2 lakh average price. Power weeders ~6–7% share, ~₹60,000 price, import-dominated. Tractors <1% national share, over 10% in <30 HP 4WD compact in Maharashtra and Gujarat; retail finance for power tillers expected to rise from ~10% to ~20%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash/investment balance and inorganic plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Investments close to ₹600 crore excluding land. Management is evaluating adjacencies globally and in India, expects to close at least one in about six months, and it will be an acquisition, not a JV.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TREM V impact on demand and what is the export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: TREM V costs are minimal below 25 HP; above 50 HP costs rise 20–30%, with volumes already down there. Interim TREM IIIA expected 2028 and full TREM V around 2032. Europe held flat as transit times rose to 90–120 days; Netherlands setup is intended to support growth this year.

Management warned further inflation would mean more price hikes and would hurt demand and volumes, and that GST-cut-driven volume may not sustain

Power weeders: ~6–7% share (entered ~2 years ago), highly unorganised and import-dominated (China), average price ~₹60,000; industry grew from ~2,000 units three years ago to ~11,500 last year

Subsidy-driven pull-forward: Maharashtra subsidy last year brought forward pent-up demand; no way to predict which state schemes come this year; central govt funds rolled out to states with flexibility on farm mechanisation and focus on small and marginal farmers
